verdict.rationale: Grafana's own docs show OpenTelemetry-based collection that claims to protect against vendor lock-in and keep data portable. Its backends ingest open standards: Tempo accepts Jaeger, Zipkin and OpenTelemetry, and Mimir ingests Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics. However, the actual ability to switch backends without re-instrumenting is only asserted, not documented as a workflow or corroborated hands-on. missing for 10: documented procedure for redirecting OTel-instrumented telemetry to a different backend without code changes, independent or hands-on corroboration of a backend switch, coverage of OTel logs/profiles portability beyond a single claim.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code

citations.quote: It helps you collect metrics, logs, traces, and profiles from your applications while protecting you from vendor lock-in and ensuring data portability
You can use Tempo with open source tracing protocols, including Jaeger, Zipkin, or OpenTelemetry.
Grafana Mimir enables users to ingest Prometheus or OpenTelemetry metrics
